comment: Section 1.3.1 identifies structural incentives that reward programme-specific delivery over shared infrastructure. The phased plan asks the first two or three programme systems to connect to the shared foundation, but does not address the first-mover problem: integration costs are borne immediately by the connecting programme while part of the value accrues later across other programmes and the wider health system.

public.text: Section 1.3.1 identifies structural incentives that reward programme-specific delivery over shared infrastructure. The phased plan asks the first two or three programme systems to connect to the shared foundation, but does not address the first-mover problem: integration costs are borne immediately by the connecting programme while part of the value accrues later across other programmes and the wider health system.
public.suggestedRevision: Add guidance for the first implementation wave: select use cases in which the connecting programme is itself a principal beneficiary, fund common integration costs centrally or through a shared transformation budget, and make reuse benefits and cost allocation explicit in the business case.
